big: In Meena's family, gold has been passed down for generations. Prices of shares have swung up and down, yet the family's gold has kept its value over the decades. But gold is not a promise, and it has not helped in every single year.

lines: My family trusts gold. Should it be a big part of my savings?
A small part can help, because gold often moves differently from shares. A big part brings its own risks. It pays no interest, and its price can stay flat for years.

rows: Keeps buying power over very long periods
Does not move in step with shares, so it can steady a portfolio
Investors buy gold in times of fear or stress
Has held value over decades, but not every year
note: Gold pays no interest or dividend. Its return comes only from a rise in its price.

title: Why hold gold
stops: Gold often moves differently from shares

caps: That difference is why a small amount can steady a portfolio.

q: Rohan's shares fall sharply while his gold holds steady. Which role is the gold playing?
why: Gold often moves differently from shares, so it can cushion a fall.
Gold pays no dividend. Its return comes only from price.
A loan to a company is a bond, and gold is not that.
A fixed deposit pays set interest, which gold does not.

q: A friend says gold is guaranteed to rise every year. What is the honest view?
opts: He is right, since gold never falls
It helped over decades, not every year
Gold is set by SEBI each year
why: Gold prices do fall in some years, so 'never' is false.
Gold does not fall in every year, either, so this is wrong.
Gold has held value over decades, yet it can stay flat for years.
SEBI does not set the price of gold in any year.

q: A war breaks out and Meena notices gold demand rising. What is this called?
why: Gold pays no dividend, so this is not what drives it.
Investors move into gold in times of fear or stress.
A premium is paid for insurance, not for gold demand.
A surveyor assesses insurance losses, with no link to gold.

q: Which is true of gold as an investment?
opts: It pays a monthly interest on holdings
It is a loan to the government itself
It gives votes in a company itself
It pays no interest, only price changes
why: Gold does not pay interest of any kind to holders.
Lending to a government is a bond, not gold.
Votes come with shares, and not with gold itself.
Gold has no interest or dividend. Its return is price change.

pts: Gold is a store of value and a diversifier, not a promise.
It pays no interest, so returns come only from price.
It has helped over decades, not in every year.
